captures.notes: The compact mass steps through several heights. Every visible room terminates in a pitched roof and every horizontal walk top uses the light authored board family rather than the former dark duplicate skin.
The reverse angle shows buildings and galleries overlapping lower circulation. Open sky and terrain belong to the settlement perimeter, not a straight core shaft.
The section exposes narrow/deep and tower parcels at staggered bases, complete roof end closures, and support ancestry beneath projecting public surfaces; no wide one-storey hut is present.
The terrain-level entrance enters a stocked market branch and immediately meets facade and route turns. There is no empty-tent substitute or uninterrupted road through the town.
From the hostile reverse ground view, facades, stocked stalls, stairs, and overhead construction interrupt the corridor before the far boundary; no broad opening reveals the core ground plane.
The transverse ground view reads as an undercroft passage bounded on both sides, with an upper layer crossing it and no direct top-to-ground shaft.
The upper public route is continuously covered by light plank assets, meets addressed facades, and has derived guards around its bounded fine-cell lightwells.
The occupied link has a pitched roof and joins inhabited endpoint masses. Dense neighboring towers partially occlude the silhouette as intended, but the link and both joins remain readable.
The underside confirms genuine occupied mass over exterior circulation rather than an unroofed floor slab. Adjacent exposed terrain lies beyond the compact edge.
All visible primary rooms, outcroppings, and occupied links have complete pitched runs and gable closures with no open room top or intersecting neighboring shell.
The top-down network shows one connected public surface with six separated guarded lightwells. No contiguous uncovered core component exceeds one macro column.
